purpose: Define a small, fast, local typed-decision architecture arm that preserves NanoJev's bounded probability contract. The arm compares the current MiniCPM5-2B LoRA + shared-prefix runtime against encoder-style and other lightweight decision models on the same owned workloads before any training or external benchmark milestone.
problem_statement: MiniCPM5-2B produced a real capability improvement over the earlier 0.6B arm, and shared-prefix inference removed most duplicate-prefix work. However, the resulting candidate is still a 2.25B decoder-oriented backbone and the heldout_v2 result remains below the promotion gate. A separate fast arm should test whether a much smaller encoder/classifier or direct-decision architecture can preserve typed-decision quality while materially reducing latency and memory.

laya.public_metadata: Convai Laya uses a ~421M bidirectional ModernBERT-large encoder plus learned decision head; English checkpoint context is 512 tokens and typed-decisions checkpoint is 1024 tokens; Apache-2.0 is publicly claimed
laya.boundary: no weights, rows, labels, outputs, calibration data, prompts or benchmark results are imported; context limits make it a speed reference, not automatically a NanoJev candidate

laya_mlx.public_metadata: mizorewww/laya-mlx is an independent Apache-2.0 MLX port reporting short-decision millisecond latency on Apple Silicon
laya_mlx.boundary: runtime ideas may be reviewed; author benchmark claims are not NanoJev evidence

required_contracts: exact revision and license recorded before any model weight download
tokenizer/model loads without trust_remote_code unless separately reviewed
state+candidate input is never truncated; models below the required context fail closed or use an independently parity-tested chunking contract
emits a normalized probability map over the exact label set; no invented confidence scalar
supports at least 12 candidates for heldout_v2 coverage and 255 candidates for the NanoJev synthetic contract, or explicitly records a cardinality limitation
temperature remains 1.0 unless a separate calibration amendment is authorized
0.9 abstention threshold is not lowered to increase coverage
CUDA-to-MPS parity is required for any trained checkpoint before heldout evaluation

compatibility_gate: zero-adapter or frozen-head parity where applicable
no network model calls during inference
diagnostic_gate: owned probe parity vs reference implementation within 1e-5 probability delta or documented rationale
accuracy, coverage@0.9, confident-wrong@0.9 and mean confidence reported by type and cardinality
p50/p95 latency, wall time, model load, forward passes, peak memory and scored tokens reported
public JevBench diagnostic may be run but remains non-promotion evidence
promotion_gate: same corpus v5 train/dev isolation as prior arms
heldout_v1/v2 read once after internal freeze
heldout_v2 protected errors and accuracy must improve over seed20 or justify a different accepted tradeoff
serial shared-prefix latency must improve materially versus seed20 without changing output semantics
official JevBench milestone remains one-shot and post-freeze

metrics: accuracy overall and by question type
mean confidence and ECE/TVD where gold distributions exist
forward passes and scored candidate-leaf tokens
risks: encoder context limits may make Laya-style checkpoints unusable for JevBench hard rows without a new chunking contract
option-marker heads may degrade above ~50 options and cannot silently reduce the 255-candidate contract
a small backbone may be faster but less accurate; speed does not override protected-error gates
MLX parity may be numerically different from PyTorch MPS and needs independent verification
pretrained decision checkpoints may be optimized for different workflows and are not evidence of NanoJev capability
